title: Drive Distance Matrix Helper: Road OD Tables
description: Build a pairwise table then validate the legs that matter by road with the Drive Distance Matrix Helper — the practical OD matrix workflow. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a four-hub US table (New York, Chicago, Dallas, Denver) starts life as straight-line kilometres here — then only the two or three legs the decision actually rides on get routed by road.
quick_answer: The Drive Distance Matrix Helper supports the working method behind origin–destination tables: build the full pairwise matrix fast from straight-line distances, then validate the important legs with real road routing. It keeps a big OD job honest without routing all hundreds of pairs before you know which ones matter.

OD matrices are a course staple. Generating the baseline table and then defending which legs deserved routing is exactly the judgement the exercise is testing.
Multi-city tours live or die on the longest legs. The matrix finds them in one glance — sort by distance and the problem children identify themselves.

Chicago–Dallas (1,295 km) and Chicago–Denver (1,478 km) rank one way on the sphere; mountain roads can narrow that gap by road. That is precisely a 'validate this leg' outcome — the helper exists to catch it.

faq: An origin–destination matrix: a table whose rows and columns are the same places, and whose cells hold the distance (or time) between each pair. It is the standard input to routing, territory and network-design work.
Why not route every pair by road?
Cost and time grow with the square of the list, and most cells never influence a decision. The professional pattern is a straight-line screen first, road truth for the legs that matter.
The ones a decision rides on: the longest, the closest-ranked alternatives, and any pair separated by terrain, water or a known bottleneck.
Yes — the pairwise table can be taken out as data for the spreadsheet or model where the study continues.
Is the straight-line table useless for road planning then?
No — it is the lower bound every road figure must exceed, and a ranking device. A road result shorter than its straight-line cell is impossible, which makes the table an error check as well.
How large a matrix is practical?
Tens of places are comfortable. Hundreds belong in GIS or a routing API batch — this helper is the screening and validation bench, not the refinery.
Does it handle one-way systems or truck restrictions?
No. Road validation here is standard routing; specialist restrictions belong in dedicated fleet tools after the screening stage.
